name: the first Target Value is adopted outright — Current Value IS it, no run, no At Target Value
a second target runs over Duration on Ease Out: the run joins at the next frame at t=0, moves on later frames, lands exactly and fires At Target Value once
because: animate-to-value.ts :166-168; timerscheduler.ts :177-194 join + onRunning(0), :132-174 t, finish, onFinish

name: Linear and Ease In give their own midpoints; a curve outside the editor's four (Ease In Quartic) is a curve all the same
because: easecurves.ts :40-42, :80-82, :86-88; animate-to-value.ts :226 looks the name up

name: a new target mid-run restarts from wherever the value is — the interrupted run never fires At Target Value; the same target again does nothing
because: animate-to-value.ts :161-168; timerscheduler.ts :43-50 start stops a running timer, :52-57 a stopped timer never finishes

name: two targets in one frame make ONE move, from where the value is, to the last (GAM-008's R-glide)
because: animate-to-value.ts :143 the description; :166-168 — the second start finds the timer queued

name: Jump To puts Current Value at Jump Value at once and carries on towards the target; the jump itself is not an arrival
a jump in the same frame as a new target, in either order, jumps and then runs from the jumped value
because: animate-to-value.ts :46-49 — the decision waits for the frame end

name: a jump onto the target stops the run and starts none: no At Target Value; a jump before any target adopts the jump as the end
NaN is ignored on both value ports; true and false are 1 and 0; numeric text is its number
Duration 0 (or below) lands on the frame AFTER the run joins — the join reads t=0, the next frame t=1 — and fires At Target Value
because: timerscheduler.ts :139-143 `duration > 0` else t = 1; :185-194 the join's onRunning(0); GAM-008 R-zero

name: Delay holds the run: no t=0 frame at the join, the value waits until now + Delay, then runs over Duration
because: timerscheduler.ts :180 `_start = now + delay`, :185 only a delay of 0 plays at once, :132 `now >= _start`

name: a Delay arriving as TEXT is concatenated onto the frame time: at time 0 '100' waits 100 ms, at time 1000 it waits until 1000100
because: animate-to-value.ts :208 stores it raw; timerscheduler.ts :180 `currentTime + timer.delay` is a string join, :132 compares it as a number (row C20)

name: a Delay written undefined (a wire let go) starts the run at NaN — a start no frame reaches: the value does not move and At Target Value does not fire, however long the clock runs, until a number reaches Delay and a new target restarts the run (C20)
because: animate-to-value.ts :208 raw; timerscheduler.ts :180 `now + undefined` is NaN, :132 `now >= NaN` is false for ever

name: Duration changed mid-run stretches the run in place: the next frame reads t against the new duration
an Easing Curve the set does not have moves along Ease Out, the default (v2; in v1 the value did not move — row C19, where the product threw and stopped every timer)
because: 'bounce' is not one of the curve set's own names; v2 reads any such name as Ease Out

name: an empty Easing Curve (a cleared field, a disconnected wire) moves along Ease Out too: half-way through the run the value is Ease Out's, not Linear's (v2, row C19)
because: '' and null are not curve names; v2 reads them as Ease Out, so at t = 0.5 the value is 8.75, where Linear would give 5. The first number is adopted outright (no run), so the 0 comes first and the run is 0 → 10
